title: Predicting TERT mutation in glioma patients using MRI-derived radiomics; A systematic review and meta-analysis

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Predicting TERT mutation in glioma patients using MRI-derived radiomics; A systematic review and meta-analysis》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Purpose · abstract-1-1】Telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter mutations are associated with malignant progression and poor survival in glioma patients. Non-invasive prediction of TERT mutation status using radiomics may provide valuable molecular insights to guide clinical decision-making. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the performance of MRI-derived radiomics-based models to predict TERT mutation in glioma patients.

【Methods · abstract-2-1】A literature search was conducted in four databases: PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and Scopus. Pooled diagnostic estimates were calculated using a bivariate random-effects model. Heterogeneity was assessed using generalized I2 statistics, and subgroup analyses were performed to investigate the source of heterogeneity. Deeks' funnel plot was used to assess publication bias.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Predicting TERT mutation in glioma patients using MRI-derived radiomics; A systematic review and meta-analysis》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · abstract-3-1】17 studies were included in the analysis. Meta-analysis yielded a pooled sensitivity of 83 % (95 % CI: 76 %-87 %), specificity of 79 % (95 % CI: 71 %-85 %), positive diagnostic likelihood (DLR) of 3.89 (95 % CI: 2.78-5.43), negative DLR of 0.22 (95 % CI: 0.16-0.30), diagnostic odds ratio of 17.56 (95 % CI: 10.57-29.16), and the area under curve of 0.88. Subgroup analysis demonstrated significant differences based on segmentation approach.

【Conclusion · abstract-4-1】MRI-derived radiomics models demonstrate good diagnostic performance for the non-invasive prediction of TERT promoter mutations in gliomas. These models may serve as an adjunctive imaging biomarker for preoperative molecular characterization and risk stratification.
